newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices lower again as US gasoline fails.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices lower again as US gasoline fails.

text.p: Oil prices lost ground for the second day in a row on Friday as rising crude supplies and the end of seasonal refinery maintenance got the better of demand increases.
London June futures for bellwether North Sea Brent blend slipped 32 cents to close at $17.97 a barrel, wiping out gains posted earlier in the week.
Dealers said a slump in the fortunes of the U.S. gasoline market triggered Friday's losses. Heating oil prices also fell sharply in the United States and Europe.
Refineries in the Western world underwent heavy repair work early in the year, cutting supplies of petroleum products. But plants are reaching full capacity again now, cutting profit margins.

U.S. gasoline demand in the approach to the peak summer driving season remains key to the short-term future of the oil markets and traders so far have been sitting on the fence on how demand will pan out.
"There's a warning here that perhaps the gasoline season might not live up to much this year," said a trader.
Brent has traded in a $1 range since its $7 three -month slide to a low of $17.54 in early April.
"The market attempted to rally early in the week and having failed is now testing the downside," said a dealer. "But for the time being I'd say $18 is a fair price in this market."
Dealers said heating oil price falls in Asia on Friday, where the market has led the world in recent weeks, has also undermined crude values.
State Indian Oil Corp (IOC) made an unexpectedly low purchase for June delivery of diesel for June. IOC bought 315,000 tonnes in seven cargoes, well below expectations of a 600,000 tonne purchase.

The eastern diesel and heating oil market still was finding support from regional trade buyer Hin Leong which, together with two other traders, had since March 3 bought almost 18 million barrels of physical gas oil.
But purchases so far this week have been slight compared to last week's one-day record of 2.44 million barrels purchased.
Speculation was that the companies were winding down their purchases.
